reason: The only cited evidence (E1) describes a different alloy (Co30Cr15Ni45Al5Ti5) and a different processing condition (annealing at 700°C for 1h), showing a uniform matrix with nano-scale Al-Ti co-enrichment and slight Co enrichment at grain boundaries. It does not provide evidence for the as-built segregation state of the target alloy, nor does it link segregation to oxidation behavior or demonstrate that homogenization improves oxidation resistance. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passage.
premises: As-built AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA exhibits local compositional segregation, especially at grain boundaries.
This segregation causes reactive element enrichment/depletion that drives non-uniform oxide scale formation and accelerated degradation.
A post-build homogenization annealing treatment can minimize these segregation effects.
Homogenization leads to a more uniform distribution of Al, Cr, and Ti.
Uniform elemental distribution promotes a coherent, adherent mixed oxide scale that improves oxidation/reduction resistance without compromising mechanical properties.
